sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 27% of the model's importance, and risk rises with it, steeply once utilization passes roughly 0.6 of the limit.
Utilization matters much more for applicants with past delinquencies: its effect grows with the number of delinquencies.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with default risk jumping once an applicant has at least one delinquency and rising further at two or more.
Income and length of credit history each have a moderate effect: default risk falls as income rises and as the credit history gets longer.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak to moderate effect, with risk increasing as the ratio rises, and it ranks fifth in importance.
Recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect, with risk rising slightly as their number grows.
Age and months at the current address hardly matter, and the number of dependents has at most a weak effect.
The data do not settle whether credit history length and recent inquiries interact.
